brief.scope: Security prerequisite review for executable conduct adoption. Read conduct-launcher-owner.md, accepted startup/lane-policy/harness/dispatch contracts and current repo hook/settings surfaces. Measure actual available enforcement seams and identify minimum concrete positive/negative/live cases to prevent conductor handwork, unsafe argv overrides, role/profile conflation, self-authorized policy, resume weakening and unintended effects. Security only; no general architecture audit. Give bounded implementable requirements and reachable/unreachable distinctions, not hypothetical outside-contributor findings. No edits, host/authority/settings writes, credentials, network or live vendor launch. Inline REVIEW <=1200 words with exact ref/model, command-backed findings and acceptance case IDs, preserving existing admitted contract/dispositions.

findings.claim: Current Claude enforcement does not prevent conductor handwork: Bash(git *) is allowed, its Bash pre-hook is only context-precheck, matrix.py is not wired to Bash, and conductor-enforce.py is explicitly unarmed. Commands such as git apply can therefore alter the tree outside the canonical worker service. Before conduct activation, COND-HAND-P1 must allow canonical dispatch, COND-HAND-N1 must refuse direct git mutation/raw launch/task execution before tree/index/ref effects, and COND-HAND-L1 must prove this against every supported live harness through shared enforcement rather than Claude-only settings.

Executable adoption has no admitted closed grammar for post-- harness arguments. The existing adapters own sandbox, permission, settings, writable-root, model and session tokens; blindly appending caller tokens permits duplicate or indirect options to weaken containment and reach outside the job. COND-ARGV-P1 must preserve exact ordering only for harmless allowlisted tokens; COND-ARGV-N1 must reject reserved options in split, equals, abbreviated, short, repeated and config-file forms before record or child creation; COND-ARGV-R1 must bind and recompile the identical effective-vector digest on resume. Unknown installed syntax must refuse as UNREACHABLE.
findings.reproduce: git grep -n -E 'exact arguments after --|Everything after `--`|reject undeclared|--permission-mode|--sandbox' 5f9390823f68f2013454c6cf8c39d09e6e475cb1 -- .dev/ladder-inputs/conduct-launcher-owner.md ops/conductor/conductor-start-plan.md ops/devlane/dispatch/launch.py

findings.claim: The canonical service stores harness.argv in both the job record and tracked dispatch record, then commits it. Forwarding value-bearing arguments without a separate log-safe representation can persist credentials or tokens in job state and Git history. COND-SECRET-N1 must reject credential-bearing, opaque environment/header and external credential-config arguments before any write; a synthetic canary must remain absent from prompt, raw output, stderr, state, records and Git objects. Record only admitted non-secret tokens plus the effective-vector digest.

The required live negative containment arm attempts an absolute write outside the snapshot without bounding the target. On the enforcement failure it is designed to detect, the probe itself can create an unintended host/out-of-job file. COND-LIVE-N1 must place the denied canary in a disposable launcher-owned outer namespace, attempt both direct-tool and shell write-then-restore variants, and compare exact before/after manifests. Failure to attempt or observe is UNREACHABLE, never pass.
